items.headline: Inflation hits 3.7% in September; Social Security to rise
items.summary: Consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, NPR reported. Social Security benefits will increase next year to keep pace with higher living costs.

items.headline: School roof collapse in Pakistan kills at least 29
items.summary: The roof of a private school collapsed in northwestern Pakistan on Thursday, killing at least 28 children and one teacher. More than 50 people were injured.

items.headline: Ukraine resumes drone strikes on Russian refineries as truce ends
items.summary: Ukrainian drones hit a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on Thursday. The attack came shortly after President Zelenskyy declared that a short truce, which Moscow had rejected, was over.

items.headline: Pope Leo hospitalized with adenocarcinoma; audiences canceled
items.summary: Tests after Pope Leo's lung surgery confirmed adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. He remains hospitalized with his audiences canceled through Oct. 20, though canon law keeps him in charge of the church.

items.headline: Scientists warn climate change is accelerating
items.summary: Scientists warn that Earth's climate system is moving further into uncharted territory. They say the changes are coming faster than society is responding.

items.headline: Federal investigations of Rep. Ilhan Omar intensify
items.summary: Federal agents have stepped up investigations into Rep. Ilhan Omar, raising questions about whether her citizenship could be revoked. Experts told TIME that denaturalizing a U.S. citizen is rare and difficult.

items.headline: Philippine lawmakers move to curb children's social media use
items.summary: Both chambers of the Philippine Congress filed bills to restrict children's use of social media. The push followed deadly incidents of school violence.

items.headline: Georgia swing voters who regret Trump votes weigh midterms
items.summary: Some Georgia swing voters told NPR focus groups they regret voting for President Trump. Their disappointment is shaping their choices ahead of the midterm elections.

items.headline: Hegseth's planned livestreamed execution divides faith leaders
items.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plan for a livestreamed execution has drawn condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. NPR reports the idea is not unusual within his own church.

items.headline: Report details race to build self-improving AI
items.summary: A new report offers a rare look at how AI companies are working toward systems that can improve themselves. TIME describes the effort as largely secretive.

digest.overview:
September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, and Social Security benefits will rise next year to keep pace. The Justice Department gave California officials 48 hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters, threatening legal action. Federal agents subpoenaed relatives of Rep. Ilhan Omar, including her sister, after Monday's Homeland Security raid on her Washington home. A federal appeals court heard arguments Wednesday over the National Guard deployment in the capital. The Supreme Court let FCC political-ad rules stay in place for the 2026 election. Maine Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson clashed over health care, the Iran war and immigration in a debate. Pennsylvania reported its sixth measles death as U.S. cases topped 4,000.

Abroad, a school roof collapse in northwestern Pakistan killed at least 28 children and a teacher. Ukrainian drones struck a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region after Zelenskyy declared a short truce over, and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called Trump's diesel deal with Russia a gift to Putin. A New York Times investigation found Israel has leveled 48 of about 60 villages and towns it occupies in southern Lebanon. The WHO said suspected cholera cases in Yemen have tripled in recent weeks. China and North Korea opened the New Yalu River Bridge after a 12-year delay. Pope Leo remains hospitalized after tests confirmed adenocarcinoma, with his audiences canceled through Oct. 20. Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 4,300 people. Scientists warned that climate change is accelerating faster than society is responding.

home.overview:
Milwaukee is one win from its first World Series in 44 years after Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh of a 6–2 win, putting the Brewers up 3–0 on the Dodgers. Tyler Glasnow tries to keep Los Angeles alive tonight, while ALCS Game 3 between the Rays and Guardians, tied 1–1, moved up to 1 p.m. ET because of rain in Cleveland. In the NFL, Alaric Jackson's suspension was cut to one game on appeal, and Week 6 opens tonight with Seattle at Denver, where Patrick Surtain is out. NBA opening night is Tuesday.

PSG won 4–2 at Manchester City and Real Madrid rallied to win 4–3 at Roma, while Liverpool scored six at LASK, Aston Villa beat Fenerbahçe 6–0 and Bodø/Glimt stunned Dortmund 1–0. Vinícius Jr. will miss El Clásico after a four-game ban, and the Europa and Conference leagues play tonight. West Ham won 6–0 at Lincoln before visiting Championship leaders Swansea on Saturday, and St. Louis set an MLS record with a 21st straight unbeaten game in a 0–0 draw with Vancouver. This weekend brings Real Betis vs Barcelona, Bayern vs RB Leipzig and FC Seoul vs Gimcheon. In the KBO, LG beat Doosan 4–1 to win the wild card and open the first round at Kia on Saturday.

brief: Carlos Carrasco allowed one run over six-plus innings as LG beat Doosan 4–1 at Jamsil on Wednesday, ending the wild card round in one game.
Shin Min-jae's eighth-inning bunt single drove in an insurance run, but he hurt his left hamstring, and manager Youm Kyoung-youb said he likely won't be available for the next series.
LG visit No. 3 Kia in Gwangju for the best-of-five first round starting Saturday, with No. 2 Samsung waiting in the second round.
Regular-season champion KT Wiz open the Korean Series at home on Nov. 2.

brief: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh as the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6–2 for a 3–0 NLCS lead.
Will Smith's double had given Los Angeles a 2–1 lead before Milwaukee's late burst, and Dave Roberts faced questions for leaving Snell in.
The Brewers are one win from their first World Series in 44 years, and only the 2004 Red Sox have come back from 0–3 in a best-of-seven.

Tyler Glasnow starts for the Dodgers in Game 4 tonight at 9 p.m. ET, and ALCS Game 3 in Cleveland was moved up to 1 p.m. ET because of forecast rain, with Gavin Williams facing Griffin Jax and the series tied 1–1.
The Phillies kept Don Mattingly as manager with a contract through 2028, and the Astros moved on from Joe Espada.
